subject: Maths
title: Scale factors
subtitle: Ratio and Proportion · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can use scale factors to enlarge or reduce shapes and interpret map scales.

key_vocab.definition: A scale factor is the multiplier that converts an original length to a new length. A scale factor greater than 1 enlarges; between 0 and 1 it reduces.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can use scale factors to enlarge or reduce shapes and interpret map scales.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: scale factor -- A scale factor is the multiplier that converts an original length to a new length. A scale factor greater than 1 enlarges; between 0 and 1 it reduces.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Scale factor = new length divided by original length. Multiply every length by the scale factor.
SF = new length ÷ original length
All lengths scale by the same factor

Key examples:
  ✓ SF = 3 means new = original × 3  (enlargement)
  ✓ SF = &frac{1}{2} means new = original × &frac{1}{2}  (reduction)
  ✓ SF = new length ÷ original length  (finding the scale factor)
  ✗ SF = 2 doubles the area  (area scales by SF² = 4)
  ✗ SF < 1 makes the shape bigger  (it makes it smaller)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – finding a scale factor
  A shape has side 4 cm. The enlargement has side 12 cm. Find the scale factor.
  SF = new ÷ original
  SF = 12 ÷ 4
  SF = 3
  SF = 3
  (Divide the new length by the original length.)

Example 2 – using a scale factor
  Enlarge a triangle with sides 3, 4, 5 cm by scale factor 2.
  Multiply each side by 2
  3 × 2 = 6, 4 × 2 = 8, 5 × 2 = 10
  New sides: 6, 8, 10 cm
  6, 8, 10 cm
  (Every side is multiplied by the same scale factor.)

sections.title: Finding scale factors
sections.content:
Find the scale factor from original to image.

(a) Original 5 cm, image 15 cm
(b) Original 8 cm, image 2 cm
(c) Original 6 cm, image 18 cm
(d) Original 10 cm, image 4 cm

sections.title: Applying scale factors
Reverse problems
sections.content:
Find the original length.

(a) New length 24 cm, SF = 4. Original?
(b) New length 5 cm, SF = &frac{1}{3}. Original?
(c) New length 30 cm, SF = 6. Original?
(d) New length 3 cm, SF = &frac{1}{5}. Original?

sections.title: Map scales
sections.content:
Use the map scale to find real distances.

(a) Scale 1 : 50 000. Map distance 4 cm. Real distance?
(b) Scale 1 : 25 000. Map distance 8 cm. Real distance?
(c) Scale 1 : 100 000. Real distance 5 km. Map distance?
(d) Scale 1 : 20 000. Map distance 12 cm. Real distance?

sections.title: Mixed scale problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) A model car is SF &frac{1}{20}. Real car is 4 m long. Model length?
(b) Sides 5, 7, 9 cm enlarged by SF 3. Find new perimeter.
(c) Photo 6 cm wide enlarged to 15 cm. Find SF.
(d) Rectangle 4 cm by 6 cm. SF = 2. Find new area.
(e) Map scale 1 : 40 000. Area on map = 2 cm². Real area?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Scale factor = new length ÷ original length
✗ A scale factor of 2 doubles the area
✓ A scale factor between 0 and 1 reduces the shape
✓ 1 : 50 000 means 1 cm on map = 50 000 cm in real life
✗ A scale factor less than 1 makes the shape bigger
